name: EyeSQUAD
summary: SQUAD driven by the eyes: a selection sphere centred where the user looks captures nearby objects, which are spread over a quad menu and narrowed down by looking at the quadrant containing the target.
howItWorks: Eye-controlled sphere-casting picks a set of objects around the stabilised point of regard; the candidates are distributed evenly over four quadrants of an out-of-context menu, and the user refines by gazing at the quadrant with the target, each step triggered by a button press, until one object remains. Compared with ray-casting and SQUAD under different target sizes and densities, EyeSQUAD outperformed previous eye-tracking selection techniques, was more accurate than ray-casting with similar speed, and was less accurate and slower than SQUAD.
advantages: Low precision demands make imprecise eye tracking usable for small targets.
limitations: Slower and less accurate than hand-based SQUAD.
Each refinement step needs a button press.

relationships.note: Slower and less accurate than SQUAD.
More accurate than ray-casting at similar speed.

review.notes: Coded from the Frontiers in VR full text. Input coded gaze; confirmation is a button press on a controller.
